title: HMS Atalanta
subtitle: Bermuda, 1880
voice_instructions: Measured, quiet, a little hushed — calm and unhurried, but with a touch more forward energy than a long documentary; the cold voice of something that read the whole file. Never sensational. Small pauses.
grade: Desaturated documentary still, a nineteenth-century Royal Navy wooden sailing ship and the open North Atlantic in winter around 1880, grey-green sea, low overcast sky, cold pale light, melancholy and uncanny, cinematic wide composition, fine film grain. Single image, not a collage, no text, no lettering, no flags with writing, no signage, no people, no faces.

beats.vo: Bermuda, January eighteen eighty. The training ship Atalanta sailed for England, with about two hundred and eighty aboard.
beats.img: A nineteenth-century three-masted Royal Navy wooden training frigate under full white sail, centred in the frame, seen side-on at a slight angle, black hull with a single white band of gunports, sailing across a grey-green sea under an overcast sky, the whole ship clearly visible and sharp, no people visible.

beats.vo: Most were young trainees. The ship never arrived. None of them was ever seen again.
beats.img: An empty stone harbour quay in England on a grey winter morning, an empty mooring berth and calm grey water, a bare iron bollard in the foreground, distant empty sea beyond the harbour mouth, no ships, no people.

beats.vo: Wreckage was reported near the Azores. None of it was ever proven to be hers.
beats.img: A single broken weathered wooden spar and a few loose planks floating on a calm grey open sea, no markings or lettering, overcast light, empty horizon.

beats.vo: A former crewman said she rolled dangerously. No trace of her was ever found.
beats.img: Inside a dim wooden ship's cabin, a brass pendulum clinometer mounted on the panelled bulkhead with its pointer swung far over to one side, a hanging oil lamp tilted at an angle, empty cabin, no people.

beats.vo: Theories include a storm, and a ship too unstable to sail. More than a century on, no wreck has ever been identified.
beats.img: A vast empty grey North Atlantic at dusk, long low swells, heavy low clouds, a faint pale break of light on the empty horizon, no ship, unresolved.

facts.claim: HMS Atalanta (ex-HMS Juno, renamed 1878), a Royal Navy training frigate (full-rigged ship), sailed from the Royal Naval Dockyard, Bermuda, on 31 January 1880 bound for England (Falmouth/Portsmouth)
About 280 aboard: sources differ — 275 (Royal Gazette/Raine), 281 named on the St Ann's Portsmouth memorial, 284 (1929 NZ press), 290 (Maritimequest); written as 'about two hundred and eighty'
Most aboard were trainees: ordinary seamen under instruction; The Times described 'some 300 lads' who had never been to sea, with only about 11 able seamen
The ship never reached England; lost with all aboard, no survivors (presumed foundered c. 12-16 February 1880)
Wreckage reported near the Azores (gunboat Avon); wreckage found over following months could not be proven/positively identified as Atalanta's
A former crew member (AS John Varling) testified she was top-heavy and rolled excessively (reported 32 degrees); the Committee of Enquiry could come to no conclusion as to the cause of the loss
Theories (as theories): foundered in a storm/gale crossing her route; inherently unstable design (David F. Raine, 1997, argues instability plus added deadweight)
No wreck has ever been identified (a sunken hulk sighted off Brittany in Sept 1880 was never confirmed as Atalanta); no 2024-2026 discovery reports found in searches on 2026-11-01
